# read-figure

Give a **text-only model** a pair of eyes — and a fixed contract for what those eyes must report.

`read-figure` is a DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that contributes exactly one tool, `read_figure`:

> Hand it the path of a figure on disk → it asks a vision model to transcribe that figure under a
> **fixed three-section protocol** → it returns the transcription as **plain text** in your context →
> you answer from it.

It does not solve the problem for you, and it should not. It does something narrower and much harder
to get right: **making "what is in this figure" clear enough to be quoted, challenged, and audited.**

---

## Why this exists

DSH can already send an *attached* image to a vision-capable model. What nobody had done is this:

- A text-only model (say `deepseek-v4-pro`) that is **given an image path** can neither see the
  image nor ask anyone who can to look at it.
- Even with a transcription, there is **no contract for its quality** — the reader cannot tell what
  was genuinely observed from what was guessed.
- Scanned exam figures routinely contain **stray black specks connected to nothing**. A human
  dismisses them as scanner noise at a glance. A text-only model cannot see the image, so it reads
  the speck as a particle, a hinge, or a label symbol — and **invents a mass that does not exist,
  invalidating the entire force analysis.**

That last point is why this plugin exists. One CPhO figure carries an isolated **3×3 px ink blob,
6 px in area**, in its upper-right corner; the problem statement itself warns
"treat it as scanner noise, not a particle." That warning is exactly what a model which cannot see
the image most needs, and most easily misses.

---

## What it produces

A fixed three-section handoff whose headings are reproduced verbatim:

```markdown
# 识图交接件 · 第 1 题

> 由 read-figure 自动生成，视觉模型 `deepseek-flash`，<timestamp>.
> 源图：`figures/1.jpg`（1536×2711px，183 KB）
> 分工：图像描述与复述由看图模型完成，物理解答由纯文本模型完成。**本文件不含任何解答。**

---

### 一、图的结构（逐项描述）
Connections → every component and its label → geometry and coordinate system. No vague wording.

### 二、复述
One paragraph of physical situation, then three lists: given / sought / conditions not in the figure.

### 三、⚠ 读图置信度声明
- **高置信**：…
- **不确定**：an isolated speck about 6×10 px at the upper right, touching no line,
  judged to be scanner noise. **If you are the text-only model reading this:
  do not introduce an extra particle or hinge because of it.**

---

## 给纯文本模型的执行说明（请一并遵守）
1. Do not fill in the figure from common sense …
2. Prefer a symbolic solution …
3. If a conclusion depends on an "uncertain" item, stop and say so …
4. Ask a follow-up list …
5. Close the answer inside the derivation sentence …
```

The protocol body is **a markdown file** (`prompts/figure-handoff.zh.md`), not strings buried in code.
Edit it directly, or point `promptFile` / `extraInstruction` at your own version —
**70% of this plugin's value is the protocol, not the few hundred lines of HTTP code.**

Three **real** outputs — verbatim, from actual runs on 2026-10-17, with only the local
absolute paths redacted — live in [`examples/`](examples/). They show both modes
(whole-figure handoff, and a targeted follow-up) and why `maxTokens` defaults to 32000:
the reasoning chain was **92.8%** of the completion on the scanned page.

---

## Install

### 1. Let the plugin manager do it (recommended — this is how the repo was verified)

Ask the agent to call `plugin_manager`, or use the equivalent CLI package operation:

```
plugin_manager install_bundle  https://github.com/Amethyst-Leafs/dsh-read-figure
plugin_manager install_bundle  ./path/to/read-figure        # a local directory, for development
```

`install_bundle` runs `pnpm add` against the profile and appends the row declared in
`cordis.patch.yml` to the profile's bundle stack — **no hand-editing of profile files**.

**Restart dsh afterwards.** Host plugins mount when the process starts, so `read_figure` only
appears after a restart. (Measured on the desktop profile: the second install returned
`application: restart-required`, i.e. nothing failed at mount time. The first attempt returned
`failed` because this package's `Config` was not a Standard Schema yet.)

### 2. Manual mount

Add one row to the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: read-figure
  name: read-figure
  config:
    model: deepseek-flash
    apiKey: sk-…            # see "Credentials" below
```

### 3. Not installed at all (zero-install evaluation)

The CLI and the plugin share every code path, so you can judge the protocol before mounting anything:

```bash
node bin/read-figure.mjs --img figures/1.jpg --img figures/2.jpg --out out/handoff.md
```

---

## Configuration

| Key | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `baseUrl` | `https://api.deepseek.com` | any OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` endpoint |
| `model` | `deepseek-flash` | vision model name |
| `apiKey` | `''` | when empty, `READ_FIGURE_API_KEY` then `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` |
| `maxTokens` | `32000` | already above the observed ceiling (~29k characters of reasoning at `effort: high` on a 3094×1526 scan); **lowering it re-creates the empty-answer bug** |
| `reasoningEffort` | `high` | `low` / `high` / `max` |
| `timeoutMs` | `180000` | per-request timeout |
| `promptFile` | `''` | empty uses the packaged `prompts/figure-handoff.zh.md` |
| `extraInstruction` | `''` | appended after the protocol, for every call in the session |
| `handoffDir` | `''` | when set, `outPath` must resolve inside it |
| `writeHandoff` | `false` | reserved: write by default |

### Credentials

A **running** DSH cannot see a shell variable exported after it started.
If an environment variable does not take effect, write `apiKey` directly into the `cordis.patch.yml` row.

---

## Using the tool

### First pass

```json
{ "imagePath": "output/…/figures/1.jpg", "label": "第 1 题" }
```

Several figures: `{"imagePaths": ["figures/1.jpg", "figures/2.jpg"], "label": "第 1、2 题"}`

### Directed follow-up

When the handoff lists an uncertainty, **do not re-run the whole transcription** — ask about it:

```json
{
  "imagePath": "figures/1.jpg",
  "question": "The longest rope hanging from B's left side — does it end at m₂ or m₃? What difference would each reading make?"
}
```

A follow-up answers that one question only, and requires the vision model to cite **position and
observed shape/pixel magnitude**. If both readings are defensible it says so, and states what
physical picture each one implies.

---

## Design notes

- **Transcribe only, never reason.** The first hard rule of the protocol is "absolutely no problem
  solving." The moment the vision model starts computing, the handoff stops being an auditable
  observation record and degrades into an answer of unknown quality that the reader can neither
  verify nor challenge.
- **Uncertainty must be listed explicitly, with a guard sentence.** Reporting "there is a speck here"
  is itself **dangerous**: without "it is noise, do not add a particle for it," a text-only model will
  take it as real. Hence the protocol demands all five parts: position, pixel size, judgement,
  reasoning, and the guard sentence.
- **False positives are more dangerous than misses.** This comes from measurement: a mechanical
  speck detector's first run reported 7 candidates on one figure, all at `x≈1` or `y≈1` — cropped
  black edges of the scan. Injected as-is, the model would believe the problem has 7 extra labels.
  **Any mechanical evidence must pass a false-positive suppression rule before an LLM sees it.**
- **Thresholds do not scale with resolution.** It is tempting to scale the pixel threshold by image
  size. Don't. `figures/2.jpg`'s stray blob (area 1139) sits squarely *between* the letterforms
  (`figures/1.jpg`'s "A" is 871, `figures/2.jpg`'s "M" is 6756) — **no area cut separates blob from
  letter.** What separates them is *small and solid*: the letters are either ≥ 70 px in one dimension
  or hollow (fill ratio ≤ 0.47). A regression test pins this: a ceiling tuned to 1.jpg (area ≤ 600)
  drops 2.jpg's blob entirely.
- **Sizes come from the file header.** "How big is that speck" is a citable fact in the h

plugins.description: Time-shifting task delegation for DeepSeek Harness (dsh): plan tasks at leisure, they run unattended off-peak, come back to a report. Human-adjudicated, desktop + web.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-lowtide **Queue tasks when it's busy. They run on their own when it's cheap.** Semi-auto or full-auto, off the model's peak hours and peak prices. A must-have plugin for DeepSeek Harness. **English** | [简体中文](./README.zh-CN.md) | [繁體中文](./README.zh-HK.md) | [العربية](./docs/README.ar.md) | [Deutsch](./docs/README.de.md) | [Español](./docs/README.es.md) | [Français](./docs/README.fr.md) | [Italiano](./docs/README.it.md) | [한국어](./docs/README.ko.md)
--- ![hero](./assets/screenshots/hero.png)

Three tasks waiting in the queue, the price status glowing in the session header, auto-run when your window opens

## Introduction lowtide is a plugin for [DeepSeek Harness (dsh)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh). The problem it solves is plain and perfectly natural: Usually, when you want an agent to do some work, you sit at the computer, send the agent an instruction, wait for the reply, and then review it by hand. But this workflow seems to forget that you have plenty of idle time — and a chance to dodge the peak/off-peak pricing that some models charge. With lowtide installed, the day goes like this: whenever a job crosses your mind during the day, toss it in the queue, glance at it, release it. The tasks pile up until the time you set (say, after 7 PM — that's when DeepSeek is at valley pricing), then run by themselves. Next morning you open the report: keep what went well, send back what didn't. That's all it is. But use it for a week and your working rhythm genuinely slows down — and don't forget, "time is money, efficiency is life"... A few key capabilities: - Four execution strategies: single, iterative, sampling, review — from "one pass is enough" to "run five candidates and I'll pick" - 168 unit tests + 10 end-to-end specs, CI green across ubuntu / windows × node 22 / 24 - One build artifact serves both desktop and web — install once, works on both - Off-peak execution lands in DeepSeek's valley hours: the same batch costs about half of what peak would ## A normal day with an agent might look like this… **Ten minutes before clocking out.** You've finished reviewing code, so you file three tickets for tomorrow: a refactor (iterative, 3 rounds), a weekly report (single), and a design you're unsure about (sampling, 4 candidates). Release them all, shut down, leave. Tomorrow at your desk, the morning report says: the refactor's done, the report's drafted, and four candidate designs sit side by side, each with its cost written out. **Friday night.** Queue a week's worth of chores in one go: dependency cleanup, missing tests, data scripts. Weekends are valley price around the clock. You go out; it works from home. Monday you check the report — retry what failed, merge what's good. **A 10 AM brainwave.** You're mid-conversation with the agent about an urgent bug when you think "hey, update the docs too." The intercept card pops up: running now costs peak price, tonight it's about half — the difference is spelled out. Click "queue for off-peak"; your draft survives untouched, and you go back to the bug. **An always-on server.** You've got a machine running dsh 24/7. Switch to L3 full-auto, then file tasks from anywhere through the API (`POST /ds-lowtide/tasks`). It runs them on schedule and writes the report. Nobody's watching, but the sandbox, the daily budget, and the file locks are all still there. **Deliverables for a client.** Use the review strategy: run once, then automatically open an independent session that tears the result apart through your chosen focus (say, "hunt for data-source errors"). In the morning you don't get a bare result — you get a result plus a critical review. **Living abroad.** You're in San Francisco; DeepSeek's peak is Beijing time, which for you lands in the evening and night before. Settings converts the official hours to your local clock, one click to adopt. You set windows by your own schedule, and the books always stay aligned with the official table. ## How lowtide works ``` ① Intake ② Adjudicate ③ Execute ④ Accept Whenever you have The queue dock When the off-peak When you're back: a moment: one-click groups tasks by window opens: five open the report — from the intercept workspace; triage preflight gates pass, results + diff card, or file a → line by line: → then sandboxed runs → + actual spend ticket (4 strategies) ✓approve ⏸defer one batch per window + money saved ✕drop / approve-all ``` A task's life: `pending-review → queued → preflight → running → done / failed / stale / timeout`, plus `deferred` (postponed) and `dropped` (soft-deleted, restorable). Step two is where lowtide differs from a "fully automated script": **every task must be released by your hand before it runs** (in L2, you release the whole batch at once, 30 minutes before the window). The machine cannot move itself into the run queue. Execution is automated; decisions are not. That's why you can safely be absent. ## A tour of the lowtide interface **The new-task modal.** Four strategies side by side, each with a plain-language hint; rounds, priority, and run mode ride along per task — no trip back to settings. Tasks land as "pending review". Nothing enters the queue without passing you. ![new-task-modal](./assets/screenshots/new-task-modal.png) **Advanced options.** Model, reasoning effort, priority from 0 to 9, fresh session or continue-previous, and the locked-files list — all in one small pane. Locked files, briefly: anything on the list gets sha256-checked before execution, and if it doesn't match what you filed, the task goes stale and refuses to run. Otherwise the file you queued against could be rewritten by another task while waiting, and this one would blindly stomp on it. ![advanced-options](./assets/screenshots/advanced-options.png) **Pick any model.** Batch runs default to the official `deepseek-flash` (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash; the retired `deepseek-v4-flash` name still routes there at Flash prices), but each task can pick its own model — anything connected to your Harness is in the dropdown, grouped by provider. Private providers work too. Non-official models have no public price table, so the ledger honestly says "price unknown"; add a price override in settings if you want the bookkeeping exact. ![model-picker](./assets/screenshots/model-picker.png) **The window editor.** Multi-segment, overnight, per-weekday — all fine. Underneath is a live 24-hour price band: red for peak, green for valley, and a marker showing where you are right now. Outside UTC+8, one click on "adopt official peak hours" converts Beijing time to your local clock. ![window-editor](./assets/screenshots/window-editor.png) **The settings page.** Window hours, tasks per batch, per-task duration cap, concurrency, daily budget, report history, autonomy level, price overrides — all graphical, no config files. The official pricing rules (including the new all-weekend valley) are explained in human language on the same page. ![settings](./assets/screenshots/settings.png) Three more pieces of UI appear in daily use: the **price pill** (session header — busy/idle, queue size; click it to edit windows), the **peak-hours intercept card** (type at peak, it appears; the price difference is spelled out; your draft survives), and the **execution report** (the morning briefing: savings first, anomalies pinned, candidates awaiting your pick, one-click Markdown copy). ## About lowtide workspaces Every task runs inside a workspace. That single dropdown decides three things. **Which files it can touch.** Tasks run in a sandbox whose boundary is the workspace directory. Pick wrong and at best it can't find the files; at worst it edits something it shouldn't. **Who it queues with.** Tasks in the same workspace run serially (two tasks never fight over one repo); different workspaces run in paralle

plugins.description: DSH Desktop 技能分组选择器：输入框内分组浏览全部技能，自动分类 + 中文说明 + 搜索，一键插入
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-skill-groups

> DSH Desktop 输入框技能选择器 —— 把散落各处的技能整理成带图标的中文分组面板，一键插入。

在 DSH Desktop 的对话输入框左侧加一枚「🧩 技能」按钮。点开是一个自绘面板：

- **双层下钻**：根页显示分类（科研写作、办公文档、数据图表……），点分类进入技能列表
- **自动分类**：显式名单优先，其余按关键词规则兜底，新装技能无需配置
- **中文说明**：三级兜底 —— SKILL.md 中文描述 → 内置中文表 → host 侧从 SKILL.md 提取摘要
- **全量技能**：host 侧合并注册表与磁盘扫描（`~/.dsh`、`~/.agents`、`~/.claude`、安装目录 office-runtime），preset 层技能也能看到
- **搜索**：面板顶部即输即滤，跨分类匹配名称与说明
- **安全插入**：走官方 `inputActions.captureInsertion / insertText` 通道，不碰草稿状态机

## 安装

DSH Desktop 插件目录布局（`web` profile）：

```
<DSH profile>/                    # %APPDATA%\dsh-desktop\harness\profiles\web
├── package.json                  # dependencies 加 "@local/dsh-skill-groups"
├── .local-plugins/
│   └── dsh-skill-groups/         # 本仓库内容
└── node_modules/
    └── @local/
        └── dsh-skill-groups -> ../../.local-plugins/dsh-skill-groups
```

`package.json` 里补两处：

```json
{
  "dependencies": { "@local/dsh-skill-groups": "file:./.local-plugins/dsh-skill-groups" },
  "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": ["@local/dsh-skill-groups"] } }
}
```

重启 DSH Desktop，输入框左侧出现「🧩 技能」即成功。

## 配置

面板行为的可调项都在 `lib/client.js` 顶部：

- `CATEGORIES` —— 分类定义（icon / label），7 类
- `EXPLICIT` —— 显式技能→分类映射，优先于关键词
- `KEYWORD_RULES` —— 兜底关键词规则，先匹配先赢
- `ZH_DESC` —— 技能名→中文一句话说明（可选，缺失时自动兜底）

host 侧 `lib/index.js` 无需配置；office-runtime 定位失败时技能照常可用，仅少 12 个内置 office 技能。

## 架构

```
client (lib/client.js)                 host (lib/index.js)
┌──────────────────────────┐   fetch   ┌────────────────────────────┐
│ 🧩按钮 + 自绘面板          │ ────────▶ │ /api/skill-picker/skills   │
│ 分类状态机 + 搜索          │           │  注册表 + 磁盘扫描合并        │
│ insertText 插入 /技能名    │           │ /api/skill-picker/describe │
└──────────────────────────┘           │  读 SKILL.md 提中文摘要      │
                                       └────────────────────────────┘
```

- client 注入点：`conversation.input.left` 插槽（session scope）
- 面板为自绘 React 组件（useState + createPortal），不受官方 slash 菜单「选中即关闭」约束
- host 数据合并策略：注册表优先，磁盘扫描按名去重补全
- `withDeadline(3000)` 兜底：host 不可达时面板仍能打开（空列表），不拖死输入框

## 卸载

删 `node_modules/@local/dsh-skill-groups` 链接、`.local-plugins/dsh-skill-groups` 目录，并移除 `package.json` 中两处条目，重启即可。

MIT

plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-deepseek-provider

DSH（DeepSeek Harness）插件：Web GUI 底部余额 pill（`conversation.composer.dock`），仅当前会话选用 DeepSeek 模型时显示，摘要展示主币种总额（优先 CNY），点击开面板看各币种总额 / 赠金 / 充值与账户可用性。数据取自 DeepSeek 开放平台 `GET /user/balance`。

## 使用方法

1. 安装：`dsh plugin --profile web add youmu129/dsh-deepseek-provider`，重启 `dsh web`（GitHub 简写规格，安装时自动装依赖；lib 构建产物已入库，无需本地构建）；
2. 凭证：默认引用 `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`（与内置 DeepSeek 路由同一把钥匙，零新增配置）；未配置时 pill 显示「未配置」；
3. 使用：DeepSeek 会话输入卡片下方出现 pill，点击弹面板看明细并手动刷新；非 DeepSeek 会话 pill 隐藏，切回即刻有数据。

凭证只经 DSH 凭证机制或环境变量存放，不入库、不写入日志与文档。

plugins.description: Plugins for DeepSeek Harness (DSH): a right-sidebar panel for chat.deepseek.com, plus plugin development notes.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-plugins

English · [中文](README.zh-CN.md)

Plugins for **[DSH](https://github.com/deepseek-ai)** (DeepSeek Harness) — and the notes I wish I had
when writing the first one.

| Plugin | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`plugins/deepseek-web-chat`](plugins/deepseek-web-chat) | A chat.deepseek.com panel in DSH's right sidebar: ask the web chat from inside the app, with workspace files or a DSH conversation attached as context. Uses your own account, no API key. |

![sign-in page](plugins/deepseek-web-chat/docs/gate-zh.png)

## Why a repo for plugins

A DSH plugin is small but not obvious: it has a **Host half** (a Cordis plugin that owns services,
HTTP routes and credentials) and a **browser half** (a bundle the DSH web UI registers as a slot),
plus a bundle patch so the loader knows the Host row. This repo keeps those pieces in one place with a
repeatable layout, tests and a reload workflow:

```
dsh-plugins/
├─ README.md / README.zh-CN.md      this page
├─ LICENSE                          MIT
├─ docs/
│  ├─ writing-a-plugin.md           how the two halves fit together
│  └─ writing-a-plugin.zh-CN.md
└─ plugins/
   └─ deepseek-web-chat/
      ├─ package.json               dsh.bundle / dsh.client declarations
      ├─ cordis.patch.yml           bundle layer: insert the Host row
      ├─ lib/                       Host (index.js, host/*) + client bundle (client.js) + web UI
      ├─ scripts/                   self-tests, smoke tests, preview server
      └─ docs/                      bilingual user guide and screenshots
```

## Quick start

Open **Plugins → Add plugin** in DSH and paste this one line:

```
github:vector-c-li/dsh-plugins#path:/plugins/deepseek-web-chat
```

DSH installs it with pnpm and enables it as a bundle; refresh the page (restart once if the sidebar
tab is missing) and open **DeepSeek Chat** from the `+` menu. The proof-of-work module is fetched on
first use, so there is nothing else to download.

Prefer a local checkout (for development)? `git clone` the repo and follow
[`plugins/deepseek-web-chat/README.md`](plugins/deepseek-web-chat/README.md#install) (English) or
[`README.zh-CN.md`](plugins/deepseek-web-chat/README.zh-CN.md#安装) (中文).

## Reading order

1. [`docs/writing-a-plugin.md`](docs/writing-a-plugin.md) — Host half, browser half, bundle patch,
   the module-cache trick that makes hot reload work, and the testing pyramid this repo follows.
2. [`plugins/deepseek-web-chat`](plugins/deepseek-web-chat) — a complete worked example: credentials,
   an HTTP route, an SSE stream, a WebAssembly dependency, drag-and-drop context, bilingual UI.
3. [`plugins/deepseek-web-chat/docs/guide.en.md`](plugins/deepseek-web-chat/docs/guide.en.md) — the
   user-facing guide.

## Conventions

- **One plugin per directory** under `plugins/`, named after its package (`dsh-<name>`).
- **Bilingual docs**: every human-facing document exists as `X.md` (English) and `X.zh-CN.md`
  (中文), each starting with a language switcher line.
- **No personal data in git**: no absolute home paths, no account identifiers, no tokens, no
  screenshots of a real account. See the checklist in the writing guide.
- **Downloaded assets stay out**: vendor blobs (like the proof-of-work module) are fetched by a
  script and listed in `.gitignore`.

## Privacy

These plugins run inside your DSH and talk to third-party services with **your** credentials. Nothing
is collected by this repository: there is no telemetry, and no server of mine is involved. Each
plugin's README has a *Privacy* section that states exactly what it stores and what leaves your
machine — read it before attaching files or conversations as context.

## Licence

[MIT](LICENSE) for the code here. Third-party material (DeepSeek's proof-of-work module, the
chat.deepseek.com API, trademarks) is covered by [`NOTICE.md`](NOTICE.md).

# 🛡️ dsh-permission-rules - **1024 store channel**: `npm i -g dsh1024` once, then `dsh1024 plugin --profile web add dsh-permission-rules` (counts toward the [deepseek1024.com](https://deepseek1024.com) install ranking). [![Gitee](https://img.shields.io/badge/Gitee-mirror-c71d23?logo=gitee)](https://gitee.com/perrylink/dsh-permission-rules) [![dshfind](https://dshfind.com/api/badge/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules?metric=downloads)](https://dshfind.com/plugins/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules?ref=badge) [![OpenSSF Scorecard](https://api.securityscorecards.dev/projects/github.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/badge)](https://api.securityscorecards.dev/projects/github.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules) **Claude Code-style declarative permission rules for DeepSeek Harness.** *Rules decide what is known. A reviewer model decides what is not.* [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![DSH plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/dsh--plugin-✅-green)](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin) [![dsh-doctor](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PerryLink/dsh-plugin-doctor/main/badges/PerryLink__dsh-permission-rules.svg)](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-plugin-doctor#verified-徽章) [![DSH Market](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/2BingLing/dsh-market/master/assets/readme/badge-top-rated.svg)](https://dsh.market/) [![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%5E22.19%20%7C%7C%20%3E%3D24-brightgreen.svg)](#) [![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/ci.yml?branch=main&label=CI)](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/actions) [![Version](https://img.shields.io/github/v/tag/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules?label=version)](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/releases) [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-permission-rules)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-permission-rules) [![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/dsh-permission-rules)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-permission-rules) [English](README.md) · [简体中文](README-zh.md) · [Español](README-es.md) · [Português](README-pt.md) · [हिन्दी](README-hi.md)
--- **📖 Ecosystem knowledge base** — measured data, not marketing: [plugin development guide · plugin-selection data · maintenance criteria](https://perrylink.github.io/dsh-plugin-guide/). ## ⭐ 如果它帮到了你 这个插件是 [DSH 插件家族](https://github.com/PerryLink)的一员（40+ 个，全部 Apache-2.0）。如果你在用，**给个 star** —— 它不会解锁任何功能，但会让下一个人在搜索里更容易找到它。 *English:* part of a 40+ plugin family for DeepSeek Harness. If it is useful, **a star helps the next person find it** — nothing is gated behind it. ## What is dsh-permission-rules? Claude Code-style declarative permission rules for DeepSeek Harness. Rules decide what is known. A reviewer model decides what is not. ![Terminal demo of dsh-permission-rules: dsh-permission-rules — deny/ask rules in one YAML file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/main/docs/assets/dsh-permission-rules-demo.png) ![Animated terminal demo of dsh-permission-rules](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/main/docs/assets/dsh-permission-rules-demo.gif) *The same run, animated.* ## Compatibility | Surface | Status | |---|---| | Harness | DeepSeek Harness `dsh-v0.2.1-alpha.1` (adapted 2026-09-22, full gate chain): its plugin config is the live settings contract — every field is declared `.volatile()`, the Loader hands `apply` a live reference per field, and a saved edit is committed into the running references WITHOUT remounting the plugin, with out-of-range values refused by the schema before anything is written. A host whose Schemastery predates `volatile()` (before 3.18.3) still mounts and runs this plugin — the fields simply stay ordinary values and the live config form is unavailable — because the marker is applied through a capability probe rather than assumed. `Session.append` on this line still cannot stamp the `ignorable` marker (its third argument is the surface-intent bag, and the envelope field survives for stored-log reads only), so the whole `0.2-alpha` line is pre-checked as unmarked and session-log audit stays disabled by default — `append` reads only `sourceEventSeqs`/`surfaceOp` and freezes the envelope, so it has no code path that could stamp the marker; the earlier `0.1.7-alpha` (adapted 2026-09-22), `0.1.5-rc.2` (adapted 2026-09-09) and `0.1.3-alpha` lines keep the same surface-only append signature, and every `0.2` prerelease is classified with them (a STABLE `0.2.x` release is left to the append probe, so a restored marker surface is adopted without a new plugin release). Those lines' log migrations refuse unclassified plugin events even when marked, so `strip` v1 audit rows before a `0.1.3-alpha` host opens the log and v2 audit rows before a `0.1.5-alpha` host migrates it (native v3 logs only need `repair`). | | Node | `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` | | Platforms | All (host + web settings client) | | Model | Any (deny/ask reasons surface through tool results) | ## What you get `dsh-permission-rules` puts an ordered **`allow` / `deny` / `ask`** rule list in front of every tool call on the `tools/pre-execute` waterfall — deterministic, instant, auditable, and written by you in plain YAML: - **`deny`** blocks the call; the rule's `reason` becomes the model-visible error. - **`ask`** rides the official approval seam (mount `dsh-auto-review` for a second-model answerer, or a human answers; with neither, the harness fails closed). - **`allow`** (and no-match) strictly delegates via `next()` — downstream listeners are never short-circuited. Every hit **and** every passthrough is audit-logged as a `permissionRules/decision` session event (log-only — nothing extra is injected into the model context). - **Rich matching** — tool-name globs (including `mcp__*`), agent-identity selectors (`main` / `subagent` / `preset:*`), argument key/value globs **or** regexes (with `!pattern` negation and an `absent` key dimension), workspace-relative path globs at **any nesting depth**, `when` host conditions (env vars, platform), and **shell command decomposition** (`argv`: command word, argument tokens, pipeline signature) for token-precise command matching. - **Built-in high-risk baseline** — a shipped deny/ask ruleset (destructive commands, privilege escalation, download-and-execute, sensitive paths) enabled by default and appended after user rules so a nearer user rule can override it; toggle with `builtin.enabled`. - **Hierarchical rule files** — optional `searchUp` merges every `.dsh/rules.yaml` from the session cwd to the filesystem root, nearest first. - **Dry-run rollout** — `enforce: false` audits what the policy *would* do while passing every call through. - **Hot reload** — Chokidar watch with debounce; a broken edit keeps the previous rules, never crashes. On a WSL host, or for a rule file under `/mnt/`, the watch switches to polling because native change events are unreliable there. - **Fail loud** — invalid YAML, unknown actions/fields, bad globs/regexes, backtracking-prone patterns, or more than `maxRules` rules fail the load. ## Rule syntax ```yaml # /.dsh/rules.yaml rules: - match: { tools: [bash, pwsh], params: { command: "git push*" }, paths: ["**/secrets/**"] } action: deny reason: "No pushes from protected paths" - match: { tools: [edit, write] } action: ask reason: "File writes need confirmation" ``` - **Match dimensions** — `tools` (globs, incl. `mcp__*`), `agents` (`main` / `subagent` / `preset:`; unknown identity never matches — fail closed), `params` (key/value globs or regexes, `!pattern` negation, `absent` key dimension), `paths` (workspace-relative globs extracted at any nesting depth), `when` (`env` var globs/regexes + a closed `platform` list), and `network` (`domains` / `ips` / `ports` / `schemes` — globs, wildcards, CIDRs, port ranges). - **Actions** — `allow` / `deny` / `ask`, evaluated in file order, first match wins. - **Rule metadata** — `enabled: false` (visible but inert), `description`, `tags`; unknown fields fail the load. - **Schema**

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin: dispatch work to DSH agents from Claude Code / Codex — native subagent progress, in-host worker sessions with per-tier presets, and a multimodal bridge that lends the text-only harness vision and image generation.
plugins.readme_text:
DSH Crew

A DeepSeek Harness plugin: dispatch work to DSH agents from Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok, without giving up the host's native subagent UI.
Native Progress UI • Tier Policy & Escalation • Dispatch Guardrails • Jobs Board • In-Host DSH Sessions • Vision & Image Gen (Native-First) • One-Click Install

npm: @zseven-w/dsh-crew · Current plugin release: 0.1.0-rc.11 · Tested with DSH 0.1.1-rc.1

English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Français · Español · Deutsch · Português · Русский · हिन्दी · Türkçe · ไทย · Tiếng Việt · Bahasa Indonesia


The DSH Crew settings page — host integrations, dispatch policy, execution and the multimodal bridge

## Why DSH Crew DSH Crew is a plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) — an open-source agent harness. It makes DSH agents dispatchable from Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and Grok: the orchestrator keeps its own model, the work runs on a real DSH agent with that harness's tools, sandbox, presets and session history, and the host still shows it as a native subagent with live progress. What runs the work is a DSH agent, not a bare model call. Tiers (`flash` / `pro`) select how much capability that agent gets from the harness's configured roster — DeepSeek V4 Flash and V4 Pro today — so a change of model in DSH needs no change here.
### 🧵 Native Progress UI Workers appear as regular subagents in Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok — dispatch count, running step, tool calls and token usage all show up in the host's own task panel, plus a claude-hud statusline segment: `⚙dsh 1▶pro 2m14s 21.7k/606 ✓3`. ### 🎚️ Tier Policy and Escalation `flash` for mechanical work, `pro` for reasoning, `effort` from `off` to `max`. `tier_policy` can clamp every dispatch to one tier at the tool layer, and `escalate_on_failure` retries a failed flash run once on pro — based on evidence, not on guessing difficulty up front.
### 🏛️ In-Host DSH Sessions With the bundle installed in a DSH profile, each worker is a first-class DSH session: visible in the Web UI, grouped by working directory, mounted with the Agent preset you choose per tier. Without DSH running, dispatch falls back to a standalone DSH runtime, so CI and headless environments still work. ### 👁️ Vision and Image Generation DSH's models are text-only. `describe_image` now prefers DeepSeek's own VL model (`deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp`) whenever a key is available, then falls back to the CLIs you already have — Claude, Codex, Grok, Antigravity — or any OpenAI-compatible API you configure. `generate_image` borrows the same CLIs' brush. Pasted images stay visible in the conversation and reach the model as text.
### 🛡️ Dispatch Guardrails Every dispatch is checked before anything spawns. Worker→worker nesting is capped at origin-chain depth 3 and cycles are refused; a second worker on a workspace another job already holds is refused with the holder's info — never silently queued. Refusals are readable errors: wait or re-scope, don't bypass. ### 📋 Jobs Board The DSH Crew panel doubles as a jobs board: every worker job — running or finished — is listed with tier, effort, live progress and tokens, held workspaces show their holders, and a job that vanishes mid-flight (e.g. a hub restart) is surfaced as an orphan ghost instead of disappearing silently.
### 🔌 Custom Providers Bring your own endpoint (Base URL + API key + models) or a local command template. Each provider has a connectivity test that checks reachability and auth, then makes one real vision call so you find out now, not mid-task. ### 📦 One-Click Install The settings page installs and updates the Claude Code plugin, the Codex role files and the Antigravity / Grok agents, skills and commands for you — marketplace registration, permission allowlist, HUD wiring, absolute paths rendered for this machine — and restores them just as easily. Every settings file is backed up first.
## How it works ``` Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok (orchestrator, keeps its own model) └─ ds-flash / ds-pro ← native subagent shell (progress shows in the host's task UI) └─ MCP: dsh_run_worker(tier, effort, cwd, worker=) ├─ worker="agy"/"grok" → that external CLI runs the task (explicit opt-in) ├─ hub reachable → session inside DSH (visible in the Web UI, grouped by cwd) └─ otherwise → dsh-jsonrpc-agent runtime (worker.cordis.yml) └─ DeepSeek V4 Flash / Pro (DSH SDK, event stream → progress and token stats) ``` ## One run, two views Dispatch fans out. Below, eighteen workers translate this README in parallel: the host counts them as its own subagents, while the harness runs them as real sessions.

Claude Code sees dsh-crew workers as native subagents, with a statusline segment tracking running tiers, elapsed time and tokens.

The DSH Crew panel sees the same run from the harness side: which host dispatched each job, its tier and effort, live progress and token usage.

The panel is also the jobs board: running and finished jobs stay listed with tier, progress and tokens, held workspaces name their holders, and a job that vanishes mid-flight (a hub restart) surfaces as an orphan ghost instead of disappearing silently.

## Install Install into a DSH profile from npm: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add @zseven-w/dsh-crew@latest dsh web ``` Or, for local development straight from the source tree: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-crew dsh web ``` The `link:` protocol symlinks the profile dependency to this repository, so rebuilds are visible immediately. ### Configure DeepSeek credentials (standalone only) In hub mode — the installation above — workers run inside the DSH instance and use the DeepSeek credentials it is already configured with. Nothing else to set up. Only the standalone fallback needs a key of its own: dispatching from a host with no DSH instance running launches a worker runtime as a separate process. Obtain an API key from [platform.deepseek.com](https://platform.deepseek.com) and write it to `~/.config/dsh-crew/.env`: ``` DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=sk-... ``` ### Verify ```bash node scripts/smoke.mjs ``` The smoke test dispatches one cheap job through whichever path is available — the hub when a DSH instance is running, s

plugins.description: Excel 角色卡：读取 .xlsx 角色档案，让 DSH 按性别、年龄、身高、性格等设定持续扮演对应角色（DeepSeek Harness 插件）
plugins.readme_text:
# Excel 角色卡

> 把一张 Excel 角色表变成 DSH 里的常驻角色：上传后，助手会按表里的性别、年龄、身高、性格、身份、说话风格等设定，以第一人称持续扮演。 仓库：[github.com/wuliao117/dsh-excel-character-card](https://github.com/wuliao117/dsh-excel-character-card) [![test](https://github.com/wuliao117/dsh-excel-character-card/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wuliao117/dsh-excel-character-card/actions/workflows/test.yml) ## 为什么需要它 想让 AI 扮演一个特定角色时，通常要先把人设贴进对话，角色一多就难以管理，换会话还会丢失。这个插件把角色档案放在 Excel 里：一张表可以写一个角色，也可以写一整组角色；导入后角色卡保存在本机，按会话启用，之后每一轮回复都会自动带上角色设定。 和“每次把设定粘进提示词”相比： - 角色表可以反复编辑、批量维护； - 角色卡只导入一次，换会话仍可复用； - 启用/停用是显式操作，不会污染普通对话； - 系统提示词会持续注入角色档案，不依赖用户每轮提醒。 ## 功能 - **两种 Excel 布局**：键值表（A 列字段、B 列内容）和角色表（第一行表头、每行一个角色）。 - **多角色**：一个工作簿可以包含多个工作表、多个角色；空白行分隔的多个键值块也会被识别。 - **中文/英文字段名**：姓名、性别、年龄、身高、体重、生日、种族、身份、外貌、性格、喜好、讨厌、恐惧、背景、动机、技能、弱点、说话风格、口头禅、关系、秘密、规则等，中英文别名都支持。 - **未知字段不丢**：表里多出来的列/键会进入“其他设定”，一起注入提示词。 - **按会话启用**：每个会话可以扮演不同角色；也可以设置全局默认角色。 - **可视化面板**：输入框右侧的「角色卡」按钮可以拖入 `.xlsx` / `.xlsm`、预览、启用、停用、删除。 - **给模型用的工具**：`excel_character_card`，支持 `list` / `import` / `preview` / `get` / `activate` / `deactivate` / `delete`。 ## Excel 怎么写 ### 方式一：键值表（推荐，适合单角色） | A 列 | B 列 | | --- | --- | | 姓名 | 林晚 | | 性别 | 女 | | 年龄 | 24 | | 身高 | 168 cm | | 身份 | 独立咖啡师 | | 外貌 | 黑色长发，琥珀色眼睛…… | | 性格 | 表面温和疏离，熟了之后话多…… | | 说话风格 | 语速偏慢，句子短…… | | 背景 | 曾在香水公司做调香师…… | | 规则 | 不要主动说出自己的秘密…… | A 列是字段名，B 列是内容。字段顺序不限，行数不限；用空白行分隔可以写多个角色（每个角色都要有“姓名”）。 ### 方式二：角色表（适合多角色） | 姓名 | 性别 | 年龄 | 身高 | 性格 | 身份 | 说话风格 | 背景 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 沈砚 | 男 | 29 | 185 cm | 冷静克制，毒舌但靠谱 | 刑警 | 低音、短句 | 因为一桩旧案从法医转做刑警 | | 阿澄 | 女 | 26 | 160 cm | 热情开朗，擅长察言观色 | 花店老板 | 语速快，爱用感叹号 | 在老街长大 | | 顾言 | 男 | 34 | 178 cm | 温和有礼，边界感强 | 心理医生 | 措辞精确、声音轻 | 曾因一次误诊离开公立医院 | 第一行是表头，之后每行一个角色。表头里不认识的列会作为“其他设定”保留。 ### 其他写法 - 横排键值：`姓名 | 林晚 | 性别 | 女 | 年龄 | 24 | 身高 | 168cm`。 - 单元格内写 `字段：内容`。 - 合并单元格：值列纵向合并时会自动填充到每一行。 - 日期：常见 Excel 日期格式会转成 `YYYY-MM-DD`。 仓库内的 [`sample/角色卡示例.xlsx`](sample/角色卡示例.xlsx) 同时包含上面两种布局，可以直接拖进面板试。 ## 安装 ### 从 GitHub 安装（推荐） ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add github:wuliao117/dsh-excel-character-card dsh --profile web ``` 装完重启 web（bundle 层栈在启动时合成）。 ### 桌面端（Electron） 桌面端 profile 由应用管理，推荐让 DSH 自己安装 GitHub bundle： > 用 `plugin_manager` 从 `github:wuliao117/dsh-excel-character-card` 安装 bundle，装完告诉我是否需要重启。 安装后如果面板没有出现，完全退出应用（含系统托盘）再重新打开。 ### 本地开发安装 ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add D:\gz\excel-character-card ``` 本地目录安装要求目录里有 `package.json#dsh.bundle` 且 `lib/` 产物已在库；本插件没有第三方运行时依赖，因此不需要额外 link SDK。装完重启 web。 ## 使用 1. 在输入框右侧点「角色卡」。 2. 把 `.xlsx` / `.xlsm` 拖进面板，或点击选择文件。 3. 在角色列表里点「启用」。面板顶部会显示“当前会话角色”。 4. 直接开始聊天；角色设定会随每一轮请求注入。 5. 想恢复普通助手：点「停用」。 也可以直接对模型说： > 读取 `D:\...\角色卡.xlsx`，导入后扮演林晚。 模型会调用 `excel_character_card`：`action=import`、`path=...`、`activate=true`。 ## 数据与隐私 - 角色卡保存在 `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\excel-character-card\state.json`（或 `$DSH_HOME` 对应目录）。 - 上传的文件只在 Host 内存中解析，不会写入其他位置。 - 角色档案会进入发给模型的系统提示词；不要在 Excel 里放 API key、密码等敏感信息。 - 插件只监听本机 DSH 的 HTTP 服务，不向外部发送数据。 ## 工具 | 工具 | 说明 | | --- | --- | | `excel_character_card` | `list` 列出角色；`import` 导入（`path`，可选 `sheet`、`activate`）；`preview` 只解析不保存；`get` 查看档案与提示词；`activate` / `deactivate` 控制当前会话；`delete` 删除。 | ## 已知限制 - 仅支持 `.xlsx` / `.xlsm`；旧版二进制 `.xls` 请先另存为 `.xlsx`。 - 单个文件上限 20 MB，最多保存 200 张角色卡。 - 角色扮演的稳定性取决于模型是否遵守系统提示词；角色卡写得越具体，效果越稳定。 - 面板按会话记录启用状态；删除角色卡会同时清理指向它的启用记录。 - 角色卡注入会占用 token；过长的背景/关系建议精简到关键信息。 ## 开发与测试 ```sh node test/parse.test.mjs node test/host.test.mjs ``` - `lib/xlsx.mjs`：零依赖 XLSX 读取（ZIP + XML + 共享字符串 + 合并单元格 + 日期格式）。 - `lib/character.mjs`：字段别名、布局识别、角色卡提取、提示词生成。 - `lib/index.js`：Host 半（工具、系统提示词、HTTP API、持久化）。 - `lib/client.js`：浏览器半（输入框按钮 + 角色卡面板）。 ## 插件管理 已装插件可用 DSH 自带的插件管理器（设置 → 插件）启停和查看；本插件是标准 `dsh.bundle` 包，卸载时移除该 bundle 即可。 ## License MIT。XLSX 解压使用 vendored [fflate](https://github.com/101arrowz/fflate)（MIT）。

plugins.description: DSH plugin — free OpenCode Zen models for DeepSeek Harness (DSH). Free LLM API, no API key needed. 在 DSH 中使用 OpenCode Zen 免费模型，无需 API key
plugins.readme_text:
# opencode2dsh **Free OpenCode Zen models, natively inside DSH (DeepSeek Harness).** No API key. No registration. No extra process. [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@opencode2dsh%2Fdsh-plugin)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@opencode2dsh/dsh-plugin) [![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/@opencode2dsh%2Fdsh-plugin)](https://github.com/FishBottle7/opencode2dsh/blob/master/LICENSE) [![node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%E2%89%A520-brightgreen)](https://nodejs.org) [![DeepSeek Harness](https://img.shields.io/badge/DeepSeek%20Harness-plugin-blue)](https://github.com/FishBottle7/opencode2dsh) English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)
--- opencode2dsh registers a native DSH `LlmAdapter` that streams directly from [OpenCode Zen](https://opencode.ai/zen)'s **anonymous free lane** — the same models OpenCode's own CLI uses without an account, served to your DSH model picker as a regular provider called `opencode2dsh`. Requests leave your machine looking exactly like traffic from the OpenCode CLI (same user agent, same correlation headers), and the model catalog stays fresh through a three-tier fallback chain. There is nothing to log into and nothing to host. ## Highlights - **Zero credential, zero setup** — the anonymous lane needs no key; install, restart, chat - **Native adapter, no sidecar** — one npm package, no child process, no binary, no local port (the legacy Go sidecar is not part of the published package; see `legacy/`) - **CLI-identical disguise** — requests carry the OpenCode CLI user agent and its session/request/project header set, derived per conversation - **Selectable thinking levels** — reasoning-capable free models expose an effort picker in DSH's model selector (declared ladders where the model metadata provides them, Off/Minimal/Low/Medium/High otherwise); Responses-only `muse-spark-*` models expose only upstream-supported effort levels, and no selection keeps the provider default - **Image input where it is declared** — image attachments are accepted for every model whose [models.dev](https://models.dev) entry lists `image` in `modalities.input`, and refused for the ones that declare `text` only; models.dev being silent falls back to the live-verified vision family - **Live catalog with a fallback chain** — live upstream list ∩ free-by-metadata, falling back to offline cache and a verified static list - **Self-healing** — fast startup retries, periodic refresh, and a written health snapshot for diagnostics - **Proper error surfaces** — upstream failures (rate limit, auth, timeout, transport) arrive in DSH as classified finish reasons, and retries stay owned by DSH ## Install **From the plugin market** (recommended, once this repo is listed there): in DSH open **Settings → Plugin Market**, search `opencode2dsh`, one-click install. **From npm**: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add @opencode2dsh/dsh-plugin ``` **From source** (build the tarball yourself): ```sh git clone https://github.com/FishBottle7/opencode2dsh.git cd opencode2dsh/packages/plugin pnpm install && pnpm pack dsh plugin --profile web add ./opencode2dsh-dsh-plugin-.tgz ``` **Verify**: restart `dsh web`, open the model picker, and pick a model from the **opencode2dsh** group. Requires DSH (DeepSeek Harness) 0.1.7 or newer with a web profile (the IP 池 settings page rides the 0.1.7 Plugins page contract); Node.js ≥ 20 (already present if DSH runs); outbound HTTPS to `opencode.ai` and `models.dev`. ## Configuration Defaults work out of the box. Override via the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`: ```yaml - id: opencode2dsh name: '@opencode2dsh/dsh-plugin' config: mode: adapter # adapter (default) | sidecar providerId: opencode2dsh refreshSeconds: 300 # catalog refresh cadence ``` | Option | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `mode` | `adapter` | `adapter`: native LlmAdapter streaming straight from Zen. `sidecar`: legacy local-agent mode, not bundled — build the agent from `legacy/agent` and pass `agentPath`. | | `providerId` | `opencode2dsh` | Provider name shown in DSH. | | `refreshSeconds` | `300` | Live catalog refresh interval. Pricing metadata refreshes every 24 h. | | `agentPath` | auto-resolved | Sidecar only: path to the agent binary. | | `agentArgs` | — | Sidecar only: extra CLI args for the agent. | | `restartDelayMs` / `restartMaxDelayMs` / `maxConsecutiveCrashes` | `1000` / `60000` / `5` | Sidecar only: restart backoff and circuit breaker. | | `firstEventMs` / `bodyIdleMs` / `responsesBodyIdleMs` | `30000` / `120000` / `300000` | Adapter only, plugin 0.3.7+: stream-liveness watchdogs, in ms (integers from `1` to `600000`). Time to the first stream event, mid-response body silence, and the body-idle floor for Responses models (`muse-spark-*`). Increase `firstEventMs` for slow cold starts. Unset keeps the defaults; restart DSH after editing. | ## How it works ``` DSH session │ harness chunks (block-start / text-delta / usage / finish …) ▼ ZenAdapter (registered LlmAdapter) │ pi-ai openai-completions stream (chat models) │ pi-ai openai-responses stream (`muse-spark-*`, Responses-only on Zen) ▼ https://opencode.ai/zen/v1 ← Authorization: Bearer public with CLI-identical headers: user-agent: opencode/… x-opencode-client, x-opencode-session, x-session-affinity, X-Session-Id, x-opencode-request, x-opencode-project ``` - **Session correlation** — session/project ids are SHA-256 derived from the conversation's first user turn (stable per conversation, non-reversible), and each request gets a fresh random id, mirroring the CLI. - **Catalog fallback chain** — S1: live `GET /v1/models`; S2: models.dev pricing metadata decides "free"; S3: a compile-time verified static list. A disk cache (~7-day TTL) covers upstream outages. - **Resilience** — the adapter registers immediately at startup; if the first catalog fetch races your network (VPN/TUN reconnects, DNS), the plugin retries on a short cadence (~1 min) before settling into the periodic refresh. - **Sidecar mode** (`mode: sidecar`, legacy) — spawns a local Go agent (a single-tenant port of [opencode2api](https://github.com/jasonxu114514/opencode2api)) on `127.0.0.1:`, token-authenticated, and registers a standard `llm-pi-ai` route. **Not part of the published package**; build it from `legacy/agent` (`go build ./cmd/agent`) and point `agentPath` at the binary. ## Health & troubleshooting The plugin writes a health snapshot after every refresh round: ``` ~/.opencode2dsh/adapter-status.json ``` ```json { "status": "ready", "total": 64, "exposed": 9, "lastError": "", "writtenAt": "2026-08-29T07:01:54.915Z" } ``` | Symptom | Likely cause & fix | | --- | --- | | `403 FreeTierError` / "OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode" | The upstream restricts free-tier clients. The plugin preserves the explanation instead of reporting an invalid API key. Use the supported OpenCode client or an official API service. | | Boot screen shows `Failed to load plugins … list slot "plugins.item" requires options.id`, or the IP 池 entry has no configuration page | Your DSH predates the 0.1.7 Plugins page contract. Upgrade DSH to 0.1.7 (latest recommended). On 0.1.6 and older the page never mounts (it is gated on `configForms.whileServed`) — model routing is unaffected. | | DSH 0.1.7/0.2 cannot start after plugin installation (`pending … settingsScope`) | Upgrade the plugin to 0.3.5. On DSH 0.2, configure IP pooling through the installed opencode2dsh row on the Plugins page. | | Only 3 models | Startup fetch raced your network; retries land within ~1 min. Check `adapter-status.json` for `lastError`. | | `lastError: "fetch failed"` persisting | Outbound HTTPS to `opencode.ai` blocked; check proxy/VPN rules. | | Rate-limit errors in chat (`429 … Endpoint is unavailable`) | The anonymous lane is quota-per-IP and free models are contended. Since the fix for [#51](https://github.com/FishBottle7/opencode2dsh/issues/51) the plugin's provider retry policy rides out 429 bursts silently (8 retries, ~1s→20s backoff, ≈90s worst case per step) instead of sur

# dsh-accountdisplayname-edit

Replaces the sidebar account label — the phone number or email DeepSeek Harness
shows at the bottom-left — with text you choose, so screenshots do not expose it.

The edit entry is a new **Edit display name** row in the account menu, the one you
open by clicking that label.

## What it does

- Replaces the account label text in the sidebar footer with a display name you set.
- Adds an **Edit display name** / **编辑显示名称** row to the account menu, directly
  under Settings.
- Opens a small editor dialog: Save, Cancel, Use default. `Enter` saves, `Esc` cancels.
- Saving an empty value restores the account's own text (the phone number or email).
- Stores the value per browser in `localStorage` under
  `dsh.account-display-name-edit.alias`.
- Display only. The account, the credentials and the profile are never read or
  changed, and the plugin makes no network requests of its own.

## Requirements

Built and verified against DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`. The host half imports nothing and the
browser half fails soft, so a build whose DOM has moved on degrades to "no alias,
no extra row" rather than an error — see [Compatibility](#compatibility).

## Install

### From the desktop app

The `desktop` profile is managed exclusively by the Electron application, so install
it there through the app's own plugin surface (Settings → Plugins, or `dshmarket`);
the CLI refuses that profile by design.

### From the CLI, for any profile the app does not own

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:AomiRaku/dsh-accountDisplayName-edit
```

There is **no build step and no `prepare` script**: the browser half is committed as
`lib/client.js`, so pnpm never asks for build approval and the install is a plain
file copy.

### Manually, which is exactly what the commands above do

1. Put the package where the profile resolves its bundles —
   `<DSH_HOME>/profiles/<profile>/node_modules/dsh-accountdisplayname-edit`.
   A directory junction/symlink to a checkout works.
2. Add this to `<DSH_HOME>/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`:

   ```yaml
   - insert:
       - id: account-display-name-edit
         name: dsh-accountdisplayname-edit
   ```

   That patch layer is watched, so it applies live — no restart needed.

## Use

1. Click the account row at the bottom of the sidebar.
2. Choose **Edit display name**.
3. Type the name you want and save. Save an empty value to go back to the
   account's own text.

## Uninstall

Remove the insert from `cordis.patch.yml` and delete the package directory. The
stored display name stays in the browser's `localStorage` until you clear it; the
plugin writes nothing else.

## How it works

A dual-face plugin whose host half does almost nothing.

- **Host half — `lib/index.js`.** Deliberately import-free. Its only job is to be a
  Loader entry, so the host's client-module scanner reads `dsh.client` from
  `package.json` and serves `./client` to the browser. With no dependencies and no
  `peerDependencies`, it cannot fail to load because of a missing, renamed or
  version-mismatched peer package.
- **Browser half — `lib/client.js`.** A hand-written single-file bundle, already in
  the `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })` form the module system serves
  verbatim, so the package needs no build. It requires only `react`, which the shell
  seeds as a platform module — which is why `react` is not a dependency either.

### Why the menu row is done in the DOM

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-settings-account` renders that menu from a hard-coded
`items` array, and its only slot (`settings.launcher`, a `single` slot) is the
launcher row itself. Occupying that slot would delete 设置 / 意见反馈 / 退出登录, which
this plugin must not do. There is no menu-item slot to add to.

So the row is appended to the **open** menu's list, cloned from a shipped row — it
therefore inherits that build's exact markup, classes and styling. Appending one
node leaves React's own children untouched, and the row is removed with the menu
because React never tracked it.

Selectors use only stable identifiers, never the hashed CSS-module class prefixes:

- the launcher is `button[aria-haspopup="menu"][data-signed-out]`, an attribute the
  account component always writes; its text node is found by the `_label` suffix
  CSS modules keeps, falling back to "the last span in the button";
- the menu is a `div[role="menu"]` that the `Menu` primitive portals to `<body>`,
  identified as the one that appeared after the launcher was activated.

### Failing soft

Every DOM probe runs inside `try`/`catch`; when a probe misses, the plugin does
nothing — it never edits another node and never throws into the shell's plugin
loader. Clearing the name hands the account plugin's own text back.

The label is written through React's own text node (`nodeValue`, not
`textContent`), so later account refreshes stay observable instead of updating a
node React no longer owns.

## Compatibility

- `dsh.client.immediately: true` is required: the plugin works through side effects
  registered when its bundle materializes, so it belongs in the boot graph's
  immediate tier.
- No `engines.dsh` range is declared, on purpose. node-semver only admits a
  prerelease version when some comparator in the range shares its exact
  `major.minor.patch` tuple and itself carries a prerelease tag, so any range would
  silently exclude a later prerelease of the harness — the failure mode the
  awesome-dsh-plugin contributing guide warns about. Failing soft is the safer
  contract here.

## Verification

```sh
npm install
npm test
```

51 checks against a real DOM (jsdom + React 18.3.1):

- `test/dom.test.mjs` — 35 checks: the bundle wrapper contract, `apply()`
  registration, label replacement, re-application after the account half re-renders,
  menu-row injection (label, icon, dropped shortcut, insertion position, shipped rows
  untouched), row activation closing the menu and opening the dialog, save and reset,
  and disposal.
- `test/robustness.test.mjs` — 16 checks over the fail-soft paths: the account row
  gone entirely, the `_label` class renamed, the collapsed rail where the avatar is
  the only span, an English locale, a menu rendered before its rows exist, no
  `document.body`, the account span replaced by a React remount, and disposal after
  the account row was removed.

It was also verified in a live DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`: the host entry reaches
`fiberPhase: active`, and the running Web GUI's slot tree lists the plugin's
`shell.overlay` entry as active, which means the host served the bundle and the page
materialized and ran it.

## Store listing

The awesome-dsh-plugin entry is ready to copy:

```text
store-entry/data/plugins/AomiRaku__dsh-accountDisplayName-edit.yml
  -> data/plugins/AomiRaku__dsh-accountDisplayName-edit.yml
```

That one file, added to a fork of
[awesome-dsh-plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin), is
the whole submission — do not edit the generated READMEs by hand.

Screenshots are optional. When you have them, add a `screenshots.json` next to
`package.json` listing 1–8 repository-relative image paths; storefronts show them in
that order and fall back to images in this README when the file is absent.

```json
["assets/screenshot-1.png", "assets/screenshot-2.png"]
```

## Known limitations

- The menu row depends on the shipped account-menu DOM. A future release that
  restructures it silently drops the row (the label replacement keeps working until
  the launcher markup changes too); nothing breaks.
- The display name lives in this browser's `localStorage`, so it is per-origin and
  not synced across machines. It never reaches the account.
- Only Simplified Chinese and English strings are bundled; the row follows the
  client locale and falls back to Chinese.

## License

MIT

# 🧪 dsh-community-bench **In-app Community Bench tab for the `dsh-score` public evidence layer.** *Reads the same public registry everyone sees. No local scoring, no telemetry, no paid rank.* [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-community-bench)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-community-bench) [![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/dsh-community-bench)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-community-bench) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![GitCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitCode-mirror-2f6feb)](https://gitcode.com/PerryLink/dsh-community-bench) [![DSH plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/dsh--plugin-✅-green)](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin) [English](README.md) · [简体中文](README-zh.md) ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-community-bench ```
--- > **Status: reference consumer / maintenance mode.** No new scoring or ranking > features. The public evidence layer is `dsh-score-index` (currently > `dsh-attention-index`; repo rename pending). ## What it shows - GOE (`E0`–`E5`) per surface. At the current snapshot: 41 rows are `E0 / unrated`, 1 row is `E2 / provisional` (a null pilot); no positive measured row. - Positive measured rows only in the quality block; prior-only rows are labelled candidates, never `#1`. - Prior, bench, coverage and **evidence completeness** (not a confidence probability). - Community attention blocks and contributor reputation. - Link to the public evidence site and a refresh button. The tab is a **consumer**: evidence and grading live in the public registry, not in this plugin. If the live registry is unreachable, it falls back to the bundled snapshot and labels it. ## Install ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-community-bench ``` Then open **Settings → Plugins → Community Bench**. ## Configuration The build injects two URLs (`scripts/build.mjs`): | Env at build time | Default | |---|---| | `BENCH_SITE_URL` | `https://perrylink.github.io/dsh-attention-index/` | | `BENCH_REGISTRY_URL` | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PerryLink/dsh-attention-index/main/data/registry.json` | If the registry is hosted elsewhere, rebuild with those variables. ## Limits - The bundled snapshot is generated from `dsh-attention-index/data/registry.json`; it is a cache, not a second scoring path. - The live fetch depends on the host allowing outbound HTTPS from the Web app; on failure the tab stays on the snapshot. - No local writes, no telemetry, no tools. ## DSH plugin family | Project | Role | |---|---| | **[dsh-score](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-score)** | Local five-dimension prior inspector | | **[dsh-score index](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-attention-index)** | Public evidence layer (E0–E5, API, signals) | | **dsh-community-bench** (this plugin) | In-app consumer | | **[dsh-kit](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-kit)** | One-command family starter | ## ⭐ 如果它帮到了你 这个插件是 [DSH 插件家族](https://github.com/PerryLink)的一员（40+ 个，全部 Apache-2.0）。如果你在用，**给个 star** —— 它不会解锁任何功能，但会让下一个人在搜索里更容易找到它。 ## License Apache-2.0.

plugins.description: Encrypted local credential vault for DeepSeek Harness (??????)
plugins.readme_text:
# 信息记录 · dsh-info-records

**为 DeepSeek Harness 准备的本机加密账密库：你维护记录，智能体在登录前按站点取用。**

> **English at a glance** — An encrypted, local-first credential vault for
> DeepSeek Harness. Manage website/app logins in a native sidebar panel; the
> `info_records` tool lets the agent look up the right account before signing in.
> Capturing credentials from chat is **opt-in**, every record can be marked
> **manual-only**, and the vault is AES-256-GCM encrypted with the data key kept
> in Windows DPAPI, the macOS Keychain, or the Linux Secret Service. Requires
> DSH ≥ 0.2.1-rc.2 and Node ≥ 22.19.

![信息记录：记录页](docs/screenshots/01-records.webp)

## 它解决什么问题

用 DSH 打开网页、登录后台、处理工单时，账号密码常常要重复输入；把密码直接发进对话，又会留在会话记录里。

信息记录把账号密码集中保存在本机，并按站点组织：

- 你可以在侧边栏 **技能中心 → 信息记录** 里新增、编辑、搜索、删除记录；
- 智能体在登录前调用 `info_records` 工具，按站点/网址取用正确的账号密码；
- 你可以在对话里明确给出「账号：… 密码：…」，让插件自动收录（**默认关闭，需手动开启**）；
- 每条记录都可以标记为 **仅手动使用**：智能体既读不到、也改不了、删不掉。

## 功能

### 记录管理

- 站点/应用、网址、用户名、密码、备注、标签。
- 搜索站点、网址、用户名、备注与标签。
- 密码默认掩码，逐条显示/复制；用户名一键复制；网址一键打开。
- 删除有就地二次确认；显示使用次数、最近更新与来源（手动 / 自动 / 智能体）。
- 支持深色/浅色主题，跟随 DSH 的 `--dsw-alias-*` 设计令牌。

### 智能体工具 `info_records`

| action | 行为 |
| --- | --- |
| `list` | 列出记录（站点、用户名、标签、id；**不返回密码**） |
| `search` | 按站点/网址/用户名/标签/备注搜索（**不返回密码**） |
| `get` | 按 id / 站点 / 网址取完整记录；返回密码（可被设置关闭）；自动标记「已使用」 |
| `save` | 新增或合并记录（需要开启自动收录） |
| `delete` | 按 id 删除，或删除唯一的站点匹配 |
| `used` | 补记一次使用 |

工具描述会要求模型：登录前先 `get`、不要向无关工具转发密码、除非用户明确要求否则不要在回复里打印密码。

### 自动收录（默认关闭）

开启后，当一条用户消息同时包含「账号/用户名…」和「密码/口令…」以及网址时，自动保存或合并成一条记录，来源标记为「自动」。同一消息只处理一次；关闭后智能体的 `save` 也会被拒绝。

> 默认关闭是有意的：密码进入对话本身就是一个需要用户明确同意的动作。
> 记录页会在关闭时显示提示与一键开启入口。

![自动收录关闭时的提示](docs/screenshots/04-auto-capture-off.webp)

### 逐条权限

每条记录有一个 **允许智能体使用** 开关（默认开）。关闭后：

- `get`、`save` 覆盖、`delete`、`used` 全部拒绝；
- `list`/`search` 只显示站点、用户名等元数据，并标记「仅手动」，备注也不返回；
- 你自己仍然可以在面板里查看、复制、编辑、删除。

![编辑记录：逐条权限](docs/screenshots/03-editor.webp)

## 快速上手

1. 打开 **信息记录 → 新增记录**，填入站点、用户名、密码，按需加网址/备注/标签。
2. 让 DSH 帮你登录时，它会调用 `info_records` 取用；你可以要求它「登录前先查信息记录」。
3. 想自动收录时，在 **设置 → 自动收录** 打开开关；不想让智能体碰的记录，编辑时关闭 **允许智能体使用**。

## 安全模型

### 加密存储

- 数据文件使用 **AES-256-GCM** 加密，随机 256 位数据密钥只用于本机。
- 数据密钥的保护方式（设置页会显示当前方式）：
  - **Windows DPAPI（CurrentUser）**：密钥包裹后存进文档，只有当前 Windows 用户能解开。
  - **macOS 钥匙串**：通过 `security` 写入/读取登录钥匙串。
  - **Linux Secret Service**：通过 `secret-tool` 使用系统密钥环。
  - **本地密钥文件（回退）**：`vault.key`，权限 0600；这是弱回退，设置页会给出警告。
- 旧版 v1 明文文档会在首次读取时自动迁移为 v2 加密文档，明文被原子替换。
- 密钥保护只调用系统自带命令（`powershell.exe`、`security`、`secret-tool`），参数仅包含随机密钥或包裹后的密钥，不含用户输入；失败信息不会回显密钥。
- 解密失败、密钥指纹不匹配或文件损坏时，**不会覆盖原文件**；损坏文件会另存为 `store.json.corrupt-<timestamp>`。
- 原子写入（临时文件 + rename），写入串行化；POSIX 上目录 0700、文件 0600。

### 诚实的边界

- **同一 OS 用户下的进程仍可解密**：智能体自己的 shell 以你的账户运行，也能调用同一个系统密钥接口。加密保护的是「文件被复制/备份/其他用户读取/磁盘被翻看」，不是「账户已被攻破」。
- **DPAPI/钥匙串绑定了用户与机器**：把 `store.json` 单独拷到另一台电脑或另一个 Windows 用户，通常无法解密。当前版本还没有便携备份/导出，迁移前请先在旧机器上手动抄录或等待后续版本。若使用本地密钥文件回退，复制整个 `info-records` 目录（含 `vault.key`）可以迁移，但保护也更弱。
- **`get` 的密码会进入该会话记录**：这是让模型代替你输入的代价。设置里的「向智能体显示密码明文」可以关闭，让智能体只看到掩码。
- **自动收录是显式选项**：默认关闭；开启后，带标签的账密会被保存，普通提及登录页不会触发。
- **不是硬件密码库**：没有主密码、硬件密钥或防内存取证能力。高价值账号建议继续使用专用密码管理器。

### 网络面

- 浏览器只通过一个同源 POST 路由 `/api/info-records/rpc` 读写，注册在 `ctx.connection.fetch` 上，由 DSH 连接层负责浏览器认证。
- 没有遥测、没有外部请求、没有 CDN 资源；所有数据留在本机。
- 面板不读取其他插件的 DOM、样式或私有状态。

## 设置

| 设置 | 默认 | 作用 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 允许智能体使用记录 | 开 | 关闭后 `info_records` 全部拒绝；逐条开关仍然生效 |
| 向智能体显示密码明文 | 开 | 关闭后 `get` 返回掩码，页面仍可显示/复制 |
| 自动收录对话中的账密 | **关** | 开启后才自动保存对话中的账密，也才允许智能体 `save` |

设置页同时显示记录数、最近写入、存储加密方式与数据文件路径（可复制）。同一组开关也注册在 **设置 → 信息记录**，不需要先找到侧边栏入口。

![设置页：加密方式与开关](docs/screenshots/02-settings.webp)

## 存储位置

```text
<DSH home>/info-records/store.json        # AES-256-GCM 密文
<DSH home>/info-records/vault.key         # 仅 fallback 方式出现
```

默认 DSH home 是 `~/.dsh`，也可由 `DSH_HOME` 指定。卸载插件不会删除数据文件。

## 兼容性

- 已在 **DSH 0.2.1-rc.2**（官方 Desktop）验证：侧边栏入口、主面板、设置页、`info_records` 工具、v1 → v2 加密迁移。
- 需要 Node.js **22.19+**。
- 插件是纯 JavaScript，无构建步骤、无运行时 npm 依赖。
- 使用 `sidebar.panellist` / `main` / `settings.section` 插槽与 `ctx.connection.fetch`、`ctx.tools`、`ctx.on` 等稳定扩展点。
- 加密回退与钥匙串路径做了跨平台实现；Windows DPAPI 已实测，macOS/Linux 的具体密钥环行为取决于系统策略（可能弹一次授权提示）。

## 已知限制

- 自动收录只识别带标签的账密（`账号：… 密码：…`，最多 3 组），不支持自由散文；其余情况可以让智能体 `save` 或手动添加。
- 没有便携导出/导入；DPAPI/钥匙串加密与当前用户、当前机器绑定。
- 没有主密码、二次验证或自动锁定。
- `list`/`search` 会向模型暴露站点、用户名等元数据（密码与仅手动记录的备注除外），这是让模型选对账号所需的最小信息。

## 开发

```text
index.js            宿主：路由、info_records 工具、自动收录、存储编排
vault.js            AES-256-GCM + DPAPI/Keychain/Secret Service/密钥文件
client.js           Web：侧边栏入口、记录页、设置页、编辑弹窗、中英文文案
cordis.patch.yml    插入 info-records 行
locale/*.json       插件管理器标题与描述
docs/screenshots/   README 截图
```

插件没有构建步骤：`index.js`、`vault.js`、`client.js` 直接加载。`client.js` 通过
`window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id: 'dsh-info-records', ... })` 注册，React 来自浏览器
模块表。

# dsh-123pan

把 [123 云盘](https://www.123pan.com/) 接进 DeepSeek Harness：**用手机号 / 邮箱 + 密码登录**，直接在 DSH 里上传、下载、浏览和管理网盘文件，并把工作区**增量备份**到云端。

不需要安装 123 云盘桌面客户端，也不需要开放平台的 appid / secret。

```
dsh 插件 ──工具/设置页──▶ 123pan-core.exe（C++ 静态链接）──▶ 123 云盘
```

网络请求、MD5、16MB 分片上传、CDN 下载、token 加密全部在 C++ 核心里完成；
插件层只用 Node.js 做参数拼装与 UI，**不依赖 Python，也不需要任何运行时**。

---

## 功能

| 功能 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 手机号 / 邮箱 + 密码登录 | 密码只用于换一次 token，不落盘 |
| **API Key / Token 登录** | 直接粘贴客户端 JWT，无需账号密码；也可用配置 `apiToken` 完全免登录 |
| token 本地加密 | Windows DPAPI，绑定当前用户 |
| 自动续期 | 每次 `status` 顺手刷新 token |
| 浏览 / 搜索 | 列目录、翻页、按文件名搜索、回收站 |
| 上传 | MD5 秒传 + 16MB 分片，进度可见 |
| 下载 | 直链 + 断点无关的单流写入，受限于 CDN 能力 |
| 直链 | 取临时签名下载链接，可给外部使用 |
| 重命名 / 移动 / 删除 | 删除默认进回收站，可再彻底删除 |
| 工作区增量备份 | 跳过未变化文件、保留目录结构、可预演 |
| 侧边栏面板 | 左侧栏「123 云盘」图标，点开就是网盘文件浏览 |
| 拖拽上传 | 把文件拖进侧栏面板（或点「选择文件」）直接上传到当前目录 |
| 拖拽下载 | 点文件行的「下载」，默认存到工作区根目录，可在面板底部改 |
| 在线预览 | 点文件名直接看文本 / 图片 / 视频 / 音频 / PDF，不用先下载 |
| 主题跟随 | 设置页与侧栏面板只用宿主主题 token，亮/暗色自动跟随 |

## 安装

### 方式一：下载 Release（推荐）

[**Releases → 下载 `dsh-123pan-vX.Y.Z.zip`**](https://github.com/cny919191/dsh-123pan/releases/latest)，解压到固定目录（例如 `D:\plugins\dsh-123pan`）。

> 这个 zip 是**插件目录**，不是安装程序，不需要运行任何 exe。

然后把它接线进 profile：

```powershell
# 1) 目录联接（不需要管理员权限）
cmd /c mklink /J "%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\<profile>\node_modules\dsh-123pan" "D:\plugins\dsh-123pan"
```

2) 编辑 `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\<profile>\package.json`，**两处都要加**：

```json
{
  "dependencies": { "dsh-123pan": "file:D:/plugins/dsh-123pan" },
  "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": ["...", "dsh-123pan"] } }
}
```

3) **完全退出** DSH（任务管理器确认 `DeepSeek Harness.exe` 全部消失）再打开。

### 方式二：从源码

```bash
# 1) 在插件目录构建核心（需要 MSYS2 ucrt64 的 g++）
cd native/core
./build.sh            # Linux/macOS 下请改用对应工具链，见下文

# 2) 从本地目录安装进 DSH profile
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add /absolute/path/to/dsh-123pan
```

在 DSH 的「设置 → 插件」里确认 `dsh-123pan` 已启用，然后打开「设置 → 123 云盘」登录。

> 详细步骤（含「装了没反应」的排查）见 [docs/USAGE.md](docs/USAGE.md) §2。

### 关于核心可执行文件

`native/core/123pan-core.exe` 是用 MSYS2 ucrt64 的 g++ 编译的**静态链接**程序：

* 只依赖 Windows 系统 DLL（`ws2_32` / `crypt32` / `shell32` / `ole32`）；
* OpenSSL **静态**编入，不需要额外 DLL，也不需要 `openssl.exe`；
* TLS 根证书在运行时从 **Windows 证书存储（LOCAL_MACHINE\ROOT）**加载，
  不依赖任何 `cert.pem`，用户机器上无需额外配置。

重新构建：

```bash
# Windows（MSYS2 ucrt64）
cd native/core && ./build.sh

# 其他平台（需自行替换 OpenSSL 与 Winsock 相关部分）
g++ -O2 -std=c++17 main.cpp api.cpp http.cpp winutil.cpp -o 123pan-core -lssl -lcrypto
```

> 核心当前实现了 Windows 传输层（Winsock + DPAPI + 证书存储）。
> 移植到 Linux/macOS 需要替换 `http.cpp` 的连接层与 `winutil.cpp` 的加密/路径部分，
> 其余 API 逻辑（`api.cpp`）与协议无关，可直接复用。

> - 给人看：**[docs/USAGE.md](docs/USAGE.md)**（安装、登录、上传下载、备份、AI 工具、常见问题、安全说明）
> - 给 Agent 看：**[AGENT.md](AGENT.md)**（上传自己生成的文件时照这个做，不要生成 .py 中转脚本）

## 两种入口

| 入口 | 位置 | 用途 |
|---|---|---|
| 侧边栏面板 | 左侧栏的云朵图标 | 日常上传/下载/浏览，支持拖拽文件 |
| 设置页 | 设置 → 123 云盘 | 登录、容量、备份、关于 |

拖拽上传的实现：浏览器无法把本地路径交给宿主，所以面板把 `File` 读成 base64
`POST /api/dsh-123pan/uploadBytes`，宿主落到临时文件后交给核心上传，用完即删。
受此限制，单个文件上限取 `maxFileBytes`（默认 200MB）。

下载目录的优先级（前面的赢）：

1. 请求里的 `out`（完整文件路径）
2. 请求里的 `dir`（目录）
3. 插件配置 `downloadDir`
4. **会话工作区根目录**（默认就是这里，例如 `D:\python`）

面板底部有「下载目录」输入框：默认**自动跟随当前工作区**。
在侧栏切换工作区后，下载目录会立刻跟着变（无需重启）。手动填一个路径后会固定下来，
点旁边的「跟随工作区」按钮即可恢复自动跟随。

> ⚠️ 核心 `123pan-core.exe` 位于工作区，通常带 **Low 完整性标签**，
> 因此它**能写工作区，但写不了** `%TEMP%`、`%USERPROFILE%\.dsh`、桌面这类 Medium 目录。
> 下载因此分两步：先直连目标；若报 `cannot open output file`，
> 改为先下到 `<工作区>\.dsh-123pan-staging\`，再由 Node 搬到目标位置（Node 两边都能写）。
> 这样"下载到 .dsh"或"下载到桌面"也能正常工作。

### 工作区跟随是怎么实现的

- **客户端**订阅会话 store，取 `retainedBy.mainView > 0` 的那个会话（即主视图正在显示的会话）的 `cwd`，
  切换工作区时它会变，面板随即重算下载目录；另有 8 秒轮询 + 窗口获得焦点时刷新兜底。
- **Host** 端 `getWorkspaceRoot()` 按「最近有活动」的会话 cwd 解析（最后一条事件时间），
  供 HTTP API 使用；都取不到才退回 `workingDirectory.defaultDirectory` / 进程 cwd。

## 给 AI / 脚本的 JSON API

插件在宿主里注册了本机 HTTP 路由，AI 不需要生成任何 `.py` 脚本，直接调即可：

```bash
# 按本地路径批量上传（推荐）
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/dsh-123pan/uploadBatch   -H 'content-type: application/json'   -d '{"files":["D:\work\a.zip","D:\work\b.txt"],"parentId":0}'

# 下载（不传 out/dir 时落到工作区根目录）
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/dsh-123pan/download   -H 'content-type: application/json'   -d '{"fileId":123,"name":"a.zip","dir":"D:\work"}'
```

完整路由：`status · login · loginToken · logout · list · mkdir · upload · uploadBytes · uploadBatch · download · preview · media(GET) · url · rename · move · trash · purge · version · diag · scan · backup · backups · forget`

状态查询：`GET`/`POST http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/dsh-123pan/status`（只接受 POST + 本机回环）。

### 直接用 API Key（免账号密码）

拿到 token 后有三种用法，选一种即可：

```bash
# 1) 验证并存入本地加密会话（一次，之后 upload/download/list 都能用）
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/dsh-123pan/loginToken \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"token":"eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs..."}'

# 2) 之后正常上传 / 下载
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/dsh-123pan/upload \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"file":"D:\\work\\a.zip","parentId":0}'
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/dsh-123pan/download \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"fileId":123,"name":"a.zip","dir":"D:\\work"}'

# 3) 或者完全不登录：profile 的 cordis.patch.yml 里配 apiToken
```

token 从哪来：已登录的 123 云盘桌面客户端日志
`%APPDATA%\123pan\log\YYYY-MM-DD.log` 里搜 `Token:Bearer eyJ...`。
也可以用 `pan123_login_token` 工具直接交给 agent。

> `loginToken` 会先调一次 `status` 验证 token 有效，再 DPAPI 落盘；
> 无效 token 直接报 401，不会生成坏会话。
> 用 `apiToken` 配置时 `status` 不会回写会话文件（配置只读）。

## 配置

在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里可以覆盖（都有默认值）：

```yaml
- id: dsh-123pan
  config:
    defaultRemoteDir: dsh-backup/my-project  # 备份默认目标
    maxFileBytes: 209715200                  # 单文件上限（200MB）
    maxFiles: 5000                            # 单次备份文件数上限
    ignoreDirs: ['.git', 'node_modules']      # 自定义忽略目录
    ignoreGlobs: ['*.log', '*.tmp']           # 自定义忽略文件名
    storeDir: ''                              # 会话与清单目录（默认 $DSH_HOME/dsh-123pan）
    corePath: ''                              # 核心 exe 路径（默认包内）
    apiToken: ''                              # 直接用 API Key 当会话（免登录）
```

| 工具 | 用途 |
|---|---|
| `pan123_login` | 手机号/邮箱 + 密码登录 |
